ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and A above. BC is the horizontal base, CA is the right slanted side, and the ant climbs upward from C along CA to A. A staircase is drawn between A and B, and below the staircase there is a dashed straight line AB. The figure labels the angle at C as 60°, and the angle at A between CA and the dashed line AB as 75°. Reasoning: In triangle ABC, ∠C = 60° and ∠A = 75°, so ∠B = 180° - 60° - 75° = 45°. By the sine theorem, CA/AB = sin45°/sin60° = (√2/2)/(√3/2) = √(2/3). The descending path is not the straight line AB, but goes along the staircase from A to B. Since the angle between AB and the horizontal BC is 45°, the total horizontal displacement and total vertical displacement of the staircase are equal, so the total length of the staircase = √2·AB. Therefore the ratio of the length of the ascending path to the descending path is CA/(√2·AB) = √(2/3)/√2 = 1/√3 = √3/3.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle ABC with straight ascending path CA, stair-step descending path from A to B, angle C = 60° between CA and CB, and angle A = 75° between CA and the dashed straight line AB underlying the stairs. Therefore angle B = 180° - 75° - 60° = 45°. Use the law of sines in triangle ABC to get CA/AB = sin45°/sin60° = sqrt(2/3). The actual descending stair path is not AB but the sum of equal horizontal and vertical components along a 45° diagonal, so its length is sqrt(2)·AB. Hence ascending/descending = CA/(sqrt(2)AB) = sqrt(2/3)/sqrt(2) = 1/sqrt3 = sqrt3/3.
